n: Ironically, the attackers became angrier after killing their brothers — and turned their vengeance on the Nephites instead, leaving the Anti-Nephi-Lehies alone for now.

f.g: Guilt redirected as anger toward others.

n: They invade the Nephite borders and destroy Ammonihah — the same event told from the Nephite side in Alma 16.
Many battles follow, in which the Lamanites are driven back and killed.
Nearly all the descendants of Amulon and the priests of Noah are killed by the Nephites.
The surviving Amulonites flee east, seize power over the Lamanites there, and burn many to death for their faith.
Many Lamanites, after their losses, remembered Aaron’s preaching, began to doubt their fathers’ traditions, and believed in the Lord. Many were converted in the wilderness.

f.g: Seeds planted earlier bear fruit later.

n: The Amulonite rulers had all such believers killed.

f.g: Persecution follows the pattern set at Abinadi’s death.

n: These martyrdoms angered other Lamanites, who began hunting and killing the Amulonites, who fled further east.
Mormon notes they are still hunted “at this day,” fulfilling Abinadi’s prophecy about the descendants of the priests who burned him.
Abinadi had said that what they did to him would be a “type” — a foreshadowing — of what was to come.

f.w: a type of things to come

n: Abinadi was the first to die by fire for his faith; many would suffer the same way.

f.w: the first that suffered death by fire

n: He prophesied the priests’ descendants would cause such deaths and would themselves be scattered and hunted like sheep without a shepherd. This was fulfilled.

f.w: as a sheep having no shepherd

n: Unable to defeat the Nephites, the Lamanites go home, and many join the Anti-Nephi-Lehies in Ishmael and Nephi.
These new converts also bury their weapons, become righteous, and keep the Lord’s commandments.
They keep the law of Moses, since it is not yet fulfilled, while looking forward to Christ and seeing the law as a symbol of his coming.
They knew salvation didn’t come from the law itself; the law strengthened their faith in Christ, and they hoped for salvation through the spirit of prophecy.

f.w: they did not suppose that salvation came by the law of Moses

n: Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and their companions rejoice greatly at their success: God answered their prayers and kept every promise.

f.w: verified his word unto them in every particular
